sections.skill: Compare the center and spread of two or more data sets

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
questions.skill: Compare the center and spread of two or more data sets
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Class A scores: 70, 75, 80, 85, 90. Class B scores: 60, 70, 80, 90, 100. Compare the centers and the spreads.
questions.prompt_markup:
Class A scores: 70, 75, 80, 85, 90. Class B scores: 60, 70, 80, 90, 100.
Compare the centers and the spreads.
questions.correct_answer: Both have mean and median 80. Class B is more spread out: its range is 40 compared with 20 (and its standard deviation is larger).
questions.grading_note: Form required: a comparison of center and of spread, with values.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
questions.skill: Compare the center and spread of two or more data sets
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Find the population standard deviation (divide by n) of 2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9.
questions.prompt_markup: Find the population standard deviation (divide by n) of 2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent form. The mean is 5; the squared deviations add to 32; 32 ÷ 8 = 4, and √4 = 2. (Dividing by n - 1 gives about 2.14.)

sections.skill: Use simulation to decide whether a difference between treatments is significant

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
questions.skill: Use simulation to decide whether a difference between treatments is significant
questions.standard_level: Probability & Statistics. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Probability & Statistics, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Plants given a fertilizer averaged 24 cm; the control group averaged 20 cm. In 1,000 random regroupings of the same plants, a difference of 4 cm or more happened 12 times. Is the difference significant? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup:
Plants given a fertilizer averaged 24 cm; the control group averaged 20 cm. In 1,000 random regroupings of the same plants, a difference of 4 cm or more happened 12 times.
Is the difference significant? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: Yes. A difference this large happened only about 1.2% of the time by random grouping alone, so chance is an unlikely explanation.
questions.grading_note: Form required: the answer with the simulated probability.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
questions.skill: Use simulation to decide whether a difference between treatments is significant
questions.standard_level: Probability & Statistics. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Probability & Statistics, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Why are subjects assigned to treatments at random in an experiment?
questions.prompt_markup: Why are subjects assigned to treatments at random in an experiment?
questions.correct_answer: So the groups are alike except for the treatment, and a difference can be credited to the treatment.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent explanation.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
questions.skill: Use simulation to decide whether a difference between treatments is significant
questions.standard_level: Probability & Statistics. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Probability & Statistics, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: In a regrouping simulation, a difference as large as the observed one happened 400 times out of 1,000. What does that suggest?
questions.prompt_markup:
In a regrouping simulation, a difference as large as the observed one happened 400 times out of 1,000.
What does that suggest?

choices.text: The difference could easily be due to chance.
The treatment definitely does not work.
The experiment had no control group.

questions.correct_answer: The difference could easily be due to chance.
questions.grading_note: 40% is not rare.

questions.correct_answer: The sample is tiny and was chosen by the company, so it is likely biased.
